entries.clue: Fund-raising body wary about appeal (7)

indicators.note: the word for wary goes round, 'about', the other piece

blocks.note: it = sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

annotation.surface: A charity is nervous about launching a fundraising appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' sits so naturally beside a fund-raising body that it reads as a donations drive; it is the old slang sense of allure.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the whole purpose of such an organisation is raising and giving money for a cause.

entries.clue: Stop moving in the main? (5,2)

blocks.note: read plainly: come to a standstill
the surface pushes 'mostly'; the setter means 'on the main', the old poetic word for the open sea

annotation.surface: Someone wonders about mostly keeping still.
annotation.walkthrough: HEAVE TO is the sailing term for bringing a ship to a halt at sea, usually by setting the sails against each other; the question mark flags the pun on 'main'.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical idiom: to heave to is to stop a vessel while at sea, which is stopping moving on the main.

entries.clue: Bachelor interrupting lively dance is one against authority (5)

indicators.note: B breaks into the dance word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

annotation.surface: A single man barges into a ceilidh and defies the organisers.
annotation.walkthrough: A reel is a fast Scottish country dance, a crossword favourite for four letters meaning dance.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who resists or rises against those in charge.

entries.clue: Expert on course revised set trip (7)

indicators.note: the letters of SET TRIP are rearranged, as a revised plan is

annotation.surface: A travel expert redoes a planned trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On course' suggests someone on a training course; it means a racecourse, where a tipster advises punters which horse to back.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by setting: the racecourse is where such a person sells supposedly expert predictions of winners.

entries.clue: One offering shock treatment? (7)

blocks.note: a person who provides a service
the surface pushes electric-shock therapy; a shock is also a thick, bushy mass of hair

annotation.surface: Someone who administers electric shocks as therapy.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'shock' as a mop of hair and the treatment is a cut and blow-dry; the question mark marks the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's job is treating heads of hair, so a shock of hair is exactly what a stylist works on.

entries.clue: Spin to grip each hot drink container (3,3)

indicators.note: the spin word holds EA inside it, as a hand grips

blocks.note: ea = each, as on price labels

annotation.surface: Some spin is applied to hold a flask of hot drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spin' and 'grip' suggest a tennis or cricket surface, but 'container' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a large heated vessel from which tea is served at church halls and events.

entries.clue: Italian is excited to tour restricted centre in northeastern European state (9)

indicators.note: the letters of ITALIAN are stirred up
the rearranged ITALIAN travels round HU
HUB is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: centre = HUB, restricted to its first two letters

annotation.surface: An Italian gets worked up about a closed-off town centre while travelling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre' looks like a middle-letters instruction; it is the synonym HUB, trimmed. 'Is' is part of the surface and joins the fodder to its indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Geographical description: a Baltic state on the northeastern edge of the European Union.

entries.clue: Odds on first piece of silver and gold in fund (7)

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of 'silver'

blocks.note: SP = starting price, the odds on a horse at the off

annotation.surface: A gambler puts silver and gold coins into a betting fund.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fund' reads as a noun, a pot of money; it is the verb, to pay for. SP is racing shorthand for the starting price.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to back an event or person with money.

entries.clue: Doctor remembers unit for paying back of expenses (13)

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: A GP recalls which hospital unit to bill for costs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person at the front of the sentence; it is a verb telling you to tamper with the next thirteen letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the formal word for repaying money someone has laid out.

entries.clue: Minute in scientific site for young farm animal (4)

indicators.note: M goes inside the lab word

annotation.surface: A tiny creature is kept in a research lab for a farm animal study.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' could be read as 'tiny'; it is the abbreviation for the time unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the young of a sheep.

entries.clue: A routine PC changed as safety measure (10)

indicators.note: the letters of A ROUTINE PC are changed round

annotation.surface: A computer's settings are altered to keep it secure.
annotation.walkthrough: PC could be the computer or a police constable; either way it only supplies two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a step taken in advance to guard against harm.

entries.clue: Some propel lethal ball of little size (6)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'propel lethal' are used

annotation.surface: Someone fires a deadly little ball.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words; the surface of firing something deadly suits an airgun pellet.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a small round ball, as of lead shot or compressed feed.

entries.clue: Brand of car and ship for titled figure (8)

blocks.note: a marque is a make of car

annotation.surface: Picking a car make and a boat to suit an aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: A marquess is a British noble ranking just below a duke; the car-and-yacht surface suits his wealth.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: one rank of the British peerage, so a person holding a title.

entries.clue: Lumbering prince rode on awkwardly with American (9)

indicators.note: the letters of RODE ON are put together awkwardly

annotation.surface: A heavy-footed prince rides clumsily beside an American companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' fits the lumbering prince in the surface, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe something heavy, slow and clumsy in movement.

entries.clue: European infiltrating field cut out as dishonest (9)

indicators.note: E gets inside the rearranged letters
FIELD CUT is put out of order

annotation.surface: A foreign agent sneaks into a mown field and is judged a cheat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' looks like one phrase meaning 'removed'; 'cut' belongs to the fodder and 'out' alone says rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: given to lying and misleading others.

entries.clue: Criminal nears trap (5)

indicators.note: the letters of NEARS are treated criminally, i.e. wrongly arranged

annotation.surface: A crook closes in on an ambush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, a crook; it is an adjective saying the letters are wrongly arranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a noose or device for catching animals.

entries.clue: Conventional items kept in a retail outlet? (5)

definitions.text: items kept in a retail outlet

blocks.note: an adjective: standard, routine, as in a hackneyed answer

blocks.clueFragment: items kept in a retail outlet
blocks.note: a noun: the goods a shop holds for sale

annotation.surface: Asking whether ordinary goods are what a shop keeps.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'stock answer' is a conventional one; a shop's stock is its inventory. The question mark flags the looser second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means standard or routine; the noun means a shop's supply of goods.

entries.clue: Sort has no end of scare by house regarding violent storm (7)

indicators.note: the word for sort lacks the letter that follows
take the last letter of 'scare'

blocks.clueFragment: Sort has no end of scare
blocks.note: sort = TYPE, minus E, the end of scare

annotation.surface: A frightened person huddles by the house as a storm rages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regarding' looks like a link to the definition, but it is ON; the definition is only 'violent storm'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, the most violent kind of storm.

entries.clue: Judges the value of site developed by friends (9)

indicators.note: SITE is developed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: mates = friends, placed by the first part

annotation.surface: Pals size up a building plot they are developing.
annotation.walkthrough: The property surface makes 'developed' look like building work; it rearranges SITE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to form a rough judgement of worth or size.

entries.clue: This person’s urge to create a favourable impact (7)

annotation.surface: Someone admits their drive to make a good impression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This person's' means the setter, and the 's is 'is', not a possessive, so it contracts to I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to make people think well of you.

entries.clue: Stare at Emily’s jacket with fancy label (7)

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside, so take Emily's outer letters
the letters of LABEL are made fancy, rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone gawps at the designer label on Emily's coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The clothing surface makes 'jacket' and 'label' a coat and its tag; the jacket is just the outside of the name.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: to look someone hard in the eye, a stare.

entries.clue: Obstruct part of path in Derbyshire (6)

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words

annotation.surface: Something blocks a footpath in the Peak District county.
annotation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county in the Midlands; it is only here to hold letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to get in the way of progress.

entries.clue: Tiny chap featured in work is source of memorably cheery outlook (8)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Tiny Tim, the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

annotation.surface: A small character in a famous work is remembered for his upbeat spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim, who says 'God bless us, every one!', is the memorably cheery child in Dickens's work, so the surface nearly defines the answer too.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a hopeful disposition that expects things to turn out well.

entries.clue: Daughter is captivated by strength in fine particles (6)

indicators.note: D is held captive inside the strength word

annotation.surface: A girl is charmed by a show of strength.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captivated' reads as charmed; here it is literal, D taken captive inside the other word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a substance ground into tiny dry grains.

entries.clue: Leaders in western industry dismiss this half-baked range (5)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next three words
only half of THIS is used

blocks.note: first letters of western, industry, dismiss

annotation.surface: Bosses of western firms reject a poorly thought-out product range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dismiss' reads as the bosses' action; it is the third leader. 'Range' is not a product line but breadth, the extent across.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: range as extent or breadth, the measure from side to side.

entries.clue: Faith in secret communication (10)

blocks.note: a private disclosure, something told on trust

annotation.surface: Someone places their trust in a private message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the two definitions, though it makes the surface read as 'faith in'. Telling someone something 'in confidence' links the two senses.
annotation.definitionFit: The word covers both trust itself and a secret entrusted to someone.

entries.clue: Dull medic is given a book (4)

annotation.surface: A boring doctor is handed something to read.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dull' looks like it describes the medic; it is the definition standing alone at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lacking colour, brightness or interest.

entries.clue: Learnt about second feature of some deer (7)

definitions.note: the definition is singular, the answer plural: a pair of antlers is one feature

indicators.note: the letters are turned about

annotation.surface: Someone studied a second characteristic of deer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it rearranges LEARNT with the S.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: branched bony growths on the heads of male deer, a feature only some have.

entries.clue: A special stop to find road surfacing material (7)

annotation.surface: Making an unscheduled stop to look for road-building supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop' fits the road surface as a traffic halt, and here it is exactly that word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the tarry mixture laid on roads and pavements.
